articleTitle: Energy Efficiency for Tactical Cloud, Edge and IoT Continuum: Helping the Military Dominate the Battlespace
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: In this paper we illustrate the adoption of IoT, Edge and Cloud technologies in Military scenarios. The different platforms can be qualitatively distinguished by the source of power used to operate them, and the reliability of that source. The grid provide the most simple and effective source, but it requires fixed installation and upfront costs in deployment, on the other hand portable power sources, or battery operated devices are fundamental to support mobility. In both cases, the optimization of the energy for sustainable operations, is an important issue. We review some research problems on this topic and two solutions that provide an optimal trade-off between the level of quality of the IoT-Edge-Cloud continuum and the its energy requirements.

articleTitle: Preventive and Predictive Maintenance of Medium Complexity Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The maintenance of medium-complexity air, land and sea drones is a very critical factor in thelogistical burden of operating these vehicles. Firstly, this paper will examine the critical points of maintenance and how these impact on military operational needs. Then we will look in detail at the balance between preventive and predictive maintenance and how to find the right balance that optimizes the burden of the activity.

articleTitle: Development and evaluation of an OFDM-based bistatic S-band SDR breadboard system for waveform analysis and RADCOM detection processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a tool for a Bistatic OFDM Software Defined S-band Radar. It is used for the analysis and optimization of RADCOM as a function of the impairments generated by the urban environment in the detection of targets. The tool is realized with low-cost COTS components and MATLAB code, which allows for customizing the transmission waveform (e.g. number of OFDM carriers, bandwidth, sample rate, PAPR) to easily test different radar techniques. The results show the Range-Doppler matrix for the detection of multiple dynamic targets, obtained by decoding the received RF message in a significant urban environment.

articleTitle: Experimental validation of supervised DPCA reciprocal filter in OFDM radar on moving platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: In this paper, we present the experimental validation of a supervised reciprocal filter-enabled Displaced Phase Center Antenna (DPCA) technique for OFDM radar systems onboard moving platforms. Our setup features a two-channel receiving array installed on a vehicle and employs an onboard OFDM transmitter as a radar illuminator. The experiments were conducted in a parking area, capturing the radar echoes from stationary and moving scatterers to assess the target detection and clutter cancellation performance. Particularly, we investigate the practical benefits of the supervised reciprocal filter on the DPCA approach for mobile OFDM radar and we compare it with matched filter (MF) and reciprocal filter (RF) based solutions. The experimental results confirm the theoretical expectations and highlight the advantages of the proposed method, particularly in scenarios with moderate clutter returns.

articleTitle: Drone Intrusions in U-Space: Risk Analysis and Modeling of Cyber-Physical Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: In Europe, the U-space framework is designed to safely manage low-altitude traffic, particularly drone activities. While most aircraft are expected to be authorized and cooperative, U-space must also address unauthorized, non-cooperative, or malicious aircraft to protect persons and goods on the ground as well as other aircraft in the airspace. Although recent methods and systems address drone physical intrusions, the combination of physical intrusion with cyber-attack requires further exploration. This paper gives an overview of drone cyber-physical intrusions. We explore two challenging scenarios that combine drone intrusion with cyber-attacks on ADS-B-like surveillance protocols: drone intrusion masked by the simultaneous appearance of multiple false intrusions and drone spoofing as an emergency helicopter. These scenarios highlight the need to enhance current defense strategies against drone intrusions in order to deal with cyber-attacks.

articleTitle: 5G Mobile Network with Blockchain, IoT and Drones Integration for Military Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The evolution of 5G mobile communication technology has made it possible to develop communication architectures for the military domain. The article analyses the impact of the use of 5G mobile technology in special military operations, the associated advantages and vulnerabilities. 5G systems have high mobility for private network configuration, it allows users to be limited to only a set of certified users, the frequency band in which they operate can be controlled, they also have adaptive and dynamic control of the radio powers used on each channel so that not to distribute radio power more than necessary. Security solutions based on blockchain technologies can be integrated into such networks, so there is much more robust security solutions needed for systems that are used in military applications. The integration of IoT sensors is native to 5G technology, thus enabling complex data fusion solutions for video information, CBRN sensors, but also dedicated drone control modules to assist the mission. The basic network infrastructure is already available from manufacturers in a single-box configuration in a military-grade version.

articleTitle: COSMIC Waveforms for Integrated Communication and Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This paper introduces COSMIC (ConnectivityOriented Sensing Method for Imaging and Communication), a new waveform design method. COSMIC waveforms are created to transmit communication symbols while maintaining an extended orthogonality condition, which allows for radio imaging of the environment. A MIMO Radar-Communication (RadCom) device transmits COSMIC waveforms from each antenna simultaneously and in the same frequency band, achieving orthogonality not through space, time, or frequency multiplexing, but through algebraic precoding. The RadCom device processes echoes coming from an extended scattering scenario to create an electromagnetic image of the environment, while also transmitting data to other network entities. This paper outlines the algebraic methods for generating COSMIC waveforms and discusses optimizing imaging and communication efficiency. Simulations show COSMIC waveforms enable precise environmental imaging with good communication performance.

articleTitle: Toward a Security Operation Center for Operational Technology in Industrial Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The integration of cyber-physical systems into critical infrastructures, such as power grids and manufacturing plants, necessitates robust security measures to safeguard Industrial Control Systems from malicious threats. Due to the unique operational demands of ICS environments, traditional IT security measures are often unsuitable. To address these challenges, we present our approach for enhancing cybersecurity in energy generation plants by correlating and consolidating alerts and logs from various monitoring devices, thereby providing real-time dashboards for anomaly and threat detection. The approach is based on the development of a platform that aids Security Operation Center (SOC) teams in monitoring operational technology within industrial networks. The paper outlines the functionalities of the platform, that will be developed within the “SOC OT Impianti Generazione Energia” (SOC-OT IGE) project.

articleTitle: AeroStim: A NASA MATB-II Evolution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Assessing cognitive performance and workload in aviation research is essential for optimizing task performance and ensuring pilot safety. This study introduces AeroStim, a novel reimplementation of NASA’s Multi-Attribute Task Battery-II (MATB-II), designed to enhance versatility and applicability in diverse research contexts. AeroStim integrates three additional exercises—a Spatial Stroop Task, a Standard Stroop Task, and an N-Back Task—along with an innovative energy bar for rapid performance assessment and minor adjustments to improve user experience. The tool’s customizability allows researchers to tailor simulations to specific needs. Validation involved 8 participants performing a series of tasks with both MATB-II and AeroStim, with cognitive workload assessed via the Bedford Workload Rating Scale. Results indicated that AeroStim provided a more balanced workload distribution, supporting the hypothesis that the added exercises create diverse and adaptable simulations. AeroStim flexibility and enhanced features make it a valuable tool for comprehensive cognitive workload and stress assessment across various research applications.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Weight Adjustment System for Aerial Video Object Recognition Using YOLOv8 with Night Vision Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This article presents an innovative system for object recognition in aerial and ground-based video, leveraging YOLOv8 with the integration of night vision capabilities. The system addresses the challenges of object detection in dynamic environmental conditions by adapting model weights in real-time based on variations in drone altitude and distance. The proposed methodology ensures high detection performance even in complex scenarios, such as changes in lighting or perspective. In experimental tests conducted on aerial and ground video representing a variety of operational scenarios, the dynamic system achieved an average precision of 89.93% and an average recall of 90.70%, significantly outperforming traditional models like YOLOv8 and VisDrone. The integration of night vision, implemented through the simulation of an image intensifier, further enhanced visibility in low-light conditions. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed dynamic system in providing a robust solution for real-time monitoring in variable operational environments.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Design of Meta-Covers for Linear Antenna Beam-Shaping
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This paper explores the expanded applications of a circular passive Huygens metasurface encasing a wire antenna. It focuses on designing a cylindrical metasurface around a dipole antenna to engineer and control the system directivity leveraging a genetic algorithm-based optimization tools. The tool's effectiveness is verified through the design of an ideal metasurface coating that introduces beamforming capabilities, validated through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Surveillance and protection of critical infrastructure with Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The growing intricacy and magnitude of critical infrastructure systems necessitate the implementation of suitable surveillance and protection measures. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have emerged as an optimal technology for bolstering these infrastructures’ security and operational efficacy. This article examines the use of UAVs of various types for surveillance and protection of critical infrastructure, the possible use of sensors to increase operational awareness, the limitations and restrictions associated with their use. Furthermore, this article will present the advantages of using such a system over a classic human-resource-based security system. Finally, the discussion turned to the potential of combining AI with UAVs and the feasibility of implementing such a combination in the surveillance and protection of critical infrastructure. The discussion noted that using UAVs offers unparalleled advantages in real-time monitoring, rapid response, and adaptability to different environments. However, the most effective and still indispensable surveillance method seems to be combining the classical model using humans for surveillance with a system based on UAVs.

articleTitle: Rule-Based Scheduling for MPARs Performing Sensing and Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Multifunction phased array radar (MPAR) is capable of performing sensing and communications by functionally grouping a phased array into tailored sub-apertures, each dedicated to a distinct task. Because of limited available resources, such as bandwidth, power aperture product, and time, it is important to properly allocate them to each sub-aperture. This article examines a rule-based task scheduling algorithm wherein communication (COM) looks are employed to fill the vacant time left by the radar tasks that are allocated first (namely, volume and cued search, update and confirmation tracking). The allocation of looks is carried out for each time slot based on task priorities; however, some tasks (i.e., volume, cued, and COM) are executed in parallel when the available bandwidth and power-aperture product (PAP) permit. Simulations conducted in scenarios demonstrate the validity of the proposed allocation strategy in terms of bandwidth utilization and time occupancy.

articleTitle: Multilinear Dynamical Systems (MLDS): Applications to Tensor Kalman Filter and Tensor LQG
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: A novel mathematical development based on tensor algebra has been applied to the Kalman Filter and to Linear Quadratic Gaussian control. This approach has been tested numerically on a swarm of satellites. Our embodiment of tensor calculus replaces the conventional matrix algebra allowing the design and evaluation of today challenging multi-agent and multi-sensors systems.

articleTitle: Automation of Translating MITRE ATT&CK Pseudocode to Executable Scripts
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The field of cybersecurity is vital for safeguarding organizational systems against advanced threats. The MITRE ATT&CK framework outlines numerous adversarial tactics and techniques. However, translating these high-level descriptions into actionable detection scripts remains challenging. In this preliminary study, we introduce an automated method for transforming MITRE ATT&CK pseudocode into operational Python scripts. Our approach effectively extracts and converts conditions, creating dependable scripts validated through extensive testing. This automation closes the gap between theoretical threat intelligence and practical application, enhancing efficiency and accuracy over manual scripting methods. Consequently, our results facilitate the rapid deployment of effective detection mechanisms, strengthening defenses against new threats. This ongoing work underscores the importance of automated tools in enhancing cybersecurity capabilities across various industries.

articleTitle: Detection of flying nano-drone signatures with a K-band FMCW radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Nano-drones are insect-like drones with a threat capability of intrusion to provide intelligence and potentially violate secure establishments and public privacy rights. They are an existing technology which is becoming increasingly more available, portable, affordable and easy to operate. As such, they represent a plausible defence and security threat. In this paper, an FMCW radar prototype operating in K-band is presented which was used to detect signatures of a flying nano drone characterised by Radar Cross Section (RCS) values below $\mathbf{- 2 5} \mathbf{~ d B}$. Results show the radar prototype was capable of successfully detecting the nano drone in flight and collecting its micro-Doppler signatures in various flying trajectories.

articleTitle: Impact of Cyberattacks on Human’s Health
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This article examines the impact of cyberattacks on human health. Different types of cyberattacks are mentioned and some examples of them are given. Most attention has been paid to the harmful effects and consequences of these attacks on human health. Finally, the possibilities and ways to protect against cyberattacks and reduce damage to people’s health, their property and important data are discussed. Important factors for reducing the risks associated with cyberattacks are the increase of people’s awareness, as well as the implementation of system protection measures. In this way, harmful effects on human health can be avoided or at least mitigated. If people become more educated in this area, cybersecurity could improve significantly.

articleTitle: Joint Estimation of Range and Velocity in FMCW Radar for Autonomous Driving
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This paper studies the joint estimation of range and velocity of a target in multi-target environments by using automotive frequency modulated continuous wave radar. First, considering the single target case, the maximum likelihood criterion is employed to convert the estimation problem into an optimization problem. In order to find the solution of this optimization problem, Newton-backtracking line search method is introduced. In the multi-target case, the parameter estimation problem is decomposed into several problems for single targets, and the joint multi-target range and velocity estimation can be accomplished based on the Newton-backtracking line search method in the relaxed iterative framework. Experiments on simulated data verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

Author Keywords: joint estimation of range and velocity

articleTitle: AI as a Tool of Disinformation in the International Arena
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: In the 21st century, information has become a strategic asset, fueling competition between governments and non-government bodies. As societies rely more on technology, manipulating information has become a weapon in international conflicts. This research will explore how Artificial Intelligence (AI), depending on its development and purpose, can be used to spread disinformation and amplify the influence of specific actors globally. The rise of hacktivist groups like Anonymous and increased utilization of the Internet and cyber resources by government agents highlight this issue. With advanced programming skills, these groups can exploit vulnerabilities in large language models (LLMs) to create and disseminate false narratives. This dual capacity for cyberattacks and disinformation campaigns magnifies their global impact. Moving beyond the debate of AI being good or evil, this article examines the real threat posed by accessible AI technologies to local and global information ecosystems. It analyzes how AI, despite its developers’ good intentions, can be misused to disrupt the flow of truthful information. The research also explores potential countermeasures and proactive approaches to mitigate AI-driven disinformation campaigns. This paper scrutinizes real-world cases and their implications to shed light on the complex interplay between AI, government, hacktivist groups, and disinformation in the international arena. This analysis will provide valuable insights for policymakers, security experts, and technologists to better prepare for and address the multifaceted challenges posed by AI as a disinformation tool.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Persistent Scatterers Detection: First Results
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: We consider the topic of multitemporal or multipass Differential Synthetic Aperture Radar Interferometry (DInSAR) for monitoring ground deformation of the built environment. A fundamental step in the processing is represented by the stage of separation of pixels corresponding to monitored Persistent Scatterers (PS) from noise pixels. PS detection is typically implemented with classical detection methods, e.g. the Generalized Likelihood Ratio Test. In this work we specifically discuss the results of first experiments for the use of Deep Learning in the PS detection.

articleTitle: Enabling Technologies for Autonomous Flight in Challenging Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Special systems must be used to support autonomous aircraft that must operate at low altitude in urban environments. These platforms could be useful for several applications, such as building inspection, package delivery. Recent geopolitical events worldwide are demonstrating that the operation of low-altitude autonomous aerial platforms shall be properly manage to guarantee overall security. Autonomy includes autonomous collision avoidance with fixed and moving obstacles, autonomous ground crash avoidance, and autonomous navigation. This paper presents several sensors and systems that can be used to build up a system configuration that provides this functionality. Advantages and drawbacks are discussed for the most diffused applications. Guidelines are derived to integrate the systems to operate typical missions.

articleTitle: UAV Security logs processing using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an evaluation of Machine Learning algorithms for security logs collected from an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) integrated in a Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) architecture. Machine Learning (ML) methodologies in the analysis of security logs presents a promising strategy for enhancing the capabilities of cybersecurity experts in addressing cyber threats. Currently, the utilization and the processing of system security logs presents a significant challenge for organizations due to its time-consuming nature and the extensive human resources required. In this study, we utilized UAV security logs generated by a publicly accessible log simulator. The investigation is focused on evaluating the efficiency of five ML algorithms: Unsupervised Support Vector Machines, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, K-nearest neighbors (KNN) and Gradient Boosting, utilizing a simulated dataset that has been pre-processed. Five use cases were examined utilizing security logs content, and our analysis revealed that Logistic Regression demonstrated exceptional performance in all the studied areas.

articleTitle: A Lens-based Graded-Index Dielectric Ring for Multibeam Radiation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The development of new communication technologies requires new directive antenna systems to improve efficiency and security. In this work, a dielectric ring based on a gradedindex permittivity profile is proposed. It consists of six lens elements homogeneously distributed over the equatorial plane of an electric dipole, which acts as feed, and converts the electric field radiated by the latter in a multibeam radiation pattern, consisting of six directive beams equally spaced as the lenses. The antenna defines a set of stable communication channels in space, by isolating the other directions in order to minimize interferences and undesired interceptions.

articleTitle: Non-Parametric Target Detection Based on Sparse Representation for Hyperspectral Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Target detection is a critical aspect in the practical application of hyperspectral images. Recently, sparse representation has garnered significant attention in this field. The underlying assumption of the sparse representation model is that each pixel can be linearly and sparsely represented by a combination of the prior target and background spectra. However, detection algorithms based on sparse representation heavily rely on preset hyperparameters, which may lead to noticeable performance degradation if not chosen appropriately. To avoid this issue, we propose a non-parametric iterative target detection algorithm that considers uninterested spectra as interference and iteratively estimates target energy while minimizing interference energy. Furthermore, our proposed method enhances the detection performance for multi-pixel targets through appropriate selection of multiple test pixels. Experimental results on real hyperspectral datasets demonstrate the superior performance of our proposed detector over its counterparts.

articleTitle: Perspectives on Directed Energy Microwaves After the First 50 Years
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The field of high power microwaves (HPM), today more appropriately termed directed energy microwaves (DE microwaves), emerged following the advent of modern pulsed power in the mid-to-late 1960s. For the first 20 years, this was a cold war competition between the United States and the Soviet Union. Following the fall of the Berlin wall and the end of the first cold war in 1991, this field became more international. Today, research in DE microwaves has expanded to Europe, South America, the Middle East, and Asia, with China being the most prolific player in the world. This paper provides a perspective and geopolitical context on where this field is today and where it may be going in the future.

articleTitle: Enhancing Performance of Deep Learning Based Non-Profiled Side-Channel Attack Using Multi-Output and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Multi-output deep learning based side-channel analysis (MO-DLSCA) has been introduced to improve the performance of non-profiled side-channel attacks (SCA) using deep learning. MO-DLSCA requires only one training process to reveal a subbyte of the secret key. In non-profiled SCA scenarios, attack techniques like Differential Power Analysis (DPA), Correlation Power Analysis (CPA), or MO-DLSCA must undergo the same process to attack different target devices, even if they share the same properties. This paper introduces a new SCA technique that leverages a multi-output deep learning neural network and transfer learning to enhance the performance of non-profiled SCA on targets with similar properties to the original target. Specifically, we demonstrate the advantage of our method in nonprofiled attacks over power traces collected from AVR XMEGA microcontrollers using ChipWhisperer. The experimental results show that our technique requires only $10 \%$ of the power traces compared to the first target to reveal the subbyte key in the second target. Additionally, the attack time for the second target is reduced significantly, approximately by a factor of 5.7, compared to the conventional MO-DLSCA technique.

articleTitle: Scalable Hardware in the Loop (HIL) System for Real-Time Swarm Drone Control Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) system for the realistic simulation of drone swarm control. The system integrates physical control modules with SITL (Software-in-the-Loop) simulation, enabling communication identical to that in actual drones. The effectiveness and scalability of the system have been confirmed by experiments conducted on six drones. The detailed architecture of the system is described, along with simulation results that demonstrate a high level of accuracy in replicating actual drone behavior. The system has broad applications in research on autonomous drone systems and practical industrial applications.

articleTitle: Multiple Target Detection in Radar Systems: A Hybrid Approach Combining EM Clustering and Sparsity-based Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of detecting multiple targets embedded in Gaussian noise with unknown range positions and angles of arrival. To this end, we introduce the signal classification model of interest resorting to the latent variable model. Meanwhile, an estimation procedure is proposed, combining the expectation-maximization algorithm with sparsity-based reconstruction method. The expectationmaximization algorithm classifies targets using the maximum a posteriori criterion, while the sparsity-based reconstruction method estimates the angles of arrival of targets utilizing sparsitypromoting prior. The estimated parameters are then applied to a decision scheme based on the Likelihood Ratio Test. Finally, numerical examples illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for classification and detection.

articleTitle: RCS of a F-35 Stealth Aircraft: Statistical Analyses of a POFACETS Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This paper analyzes the simulated radar cross section (RCS) of the POFACETS F-35 aircraft model versus azimuth and elevation aspect angle. In particular, the RCS values are obtained for all azimuths and for a short-range (SR) elevation regime. Moreover, the tests are conducted considering three different frequencies of the transmitted wave, viz. 0.3 GHz (VHF), $1 \mathrm{GHz}(\mathrm{L})$, and $10 \mathrm{GHz}(\mathrm{X})$. The RCS data for the $\mathbf{F - 3 5}$ aircraft are derived through a realistic model implemented in the Mathworks Matlab simulation toolbox POFACETS, developed at the Naval Postgraduate School of the USN. Therefore, a statistical analysis of the simulated RCSs is performed to establish among which is the best theoretical model representing these data. In this respect, the parameters for the theoretical distribution are selected using the moment matching technique. Then, the best fit statistical distribution is selected as the one minimizing the Cramèr-von Mises (CVM) distance from the empirical one. Finally, the spatial autocorrelation function is also derived to evaluate the degree of spatial decorrelation under each elevation regime and operative frequency.

articleTitle: Analysis of Artificial Intelligence subject results by gender
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence is slowly becoming a part of our everyday life, so it is very important that university students learn about its developmental stages, how it works and how to create a program that builds a neural network based on the given data to play a role in decision support. Last semester, a course was offered to full-time students. Previous experience in higher education has shown that there is sometimes a significant gender difference in the results achieved. In this article, we perform a statistical analysis of the grades achieved in the Artificial Intelligence course, both in terms of theoretical lectures and programming practice.

articleTitle: Deceptiv e Jamming against SAR via Range-Azimuth Two-Dimensional Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This paper aims to achieve deceptive jamming against Synthetic aperture radar (SAR), which is of significance in electronic warfare. At the modeling stage, a SAR deceptive jamming scheme is developed by introducing range-azimuth twodimensional modulation to generate multiple false targets. In addition, an active cancellation is employed to eliminate the true target. In this context, the range and azimuth positions of false targets can be accurately manipulated through the design of corresponding modulation terms. Moreover, the number of false targets can be determined by setting transmit elements. Finally, after applying the range-Doppler (RD) algorithm with the victim SAR, the high-resolution imaging with multiple false targets can be obtained. Simulation results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed scheme for SAR jamming in terms of different system parameters.

articleTitle: Space enabled secure quantum communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The development of quantum technologies is every day more evident, translating from purely research topics to industrial applications. This represents both a threat and an opportunity to the cybersecurity technologies. Current cybersecurity methods based on computationally secure algorithms are left exposed to violation by quantum algorithms. Quantum communication provides the mean for a new level of security, unbreakable even by a party with infinite resources, the so-called Information-Theoretic Security (ITS). Space offers the perfect communication mean for quantum technologies, avoiding the technical and operational limitations to link distances inherently present in terrestrial infrastructure. Furthermore, the development of a Quantum Information Network can open the possibilities for diverse applications, such as distributed quantum computing and quantum sensing. This paper outlines the role and primary advantages of a space-based quantum communication infrastructure, delving into the essential architectural and technological aspects that have been the focus of Thales Alenia Space Italia. The emphasis is on designing and sizing solutions based on satellite constellations, as well as creating the necessary subsystems to support future constellation designs and address existing technological challenges in space applications. Specifically, the article covers the development of constellations related to quantum-enabled cryptography. It also addresses architectures and critical components, with a focus on payload enabling subsystems and related functionalities such as onboard processors and synchronization solutions.

articleTitle: The Impact of 3D Printing on the Defense Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: In the defense and security industries, additive manufacturing has been on the menu for decades. However, it is only recently that additive technologies have been able to provide viable production applications for military and security actors. Today’s militaries rely heavily on support personnel and supply chains. Modern weapons systems and technologies are much more capable than ever, meaning fewer combatants are required to deliver the same impact. At the same time, the complexity of effective and advanced technologies often requires extensive preventative maintenance from trained technicians. This is to keep them operational in peacetime. In addition to defense support personnel, the private sector provides a broader layer of support in the initial development and manufacturing of weapons and technologies, as well as upgrades and maintenance. With such a strong focus on R&D, manufacturing, maintenance, and logistics, it is no surprise that 3D printers have become an essential tool for defense and security manufacturers. 3D printing has revolutionized numerous industries, including the military sector. 3D printing offers the army an exciting opportunity to enhance its operational capabilities by revolutionizing parts production for large pieces of military equipment. The new concept could significantly reduce lead times and improve the supply chain for military equipment parts by replacing traditional forging and casting methods. In this paper, we will discuss how the use of 3D printing in the military and defense field has become so widespread and show how 3D printing technology has played a role in warfare in recent years, especially in Ukraine and Myanmar.

articleTitle: An Analysis of the Feasibility of Providing On-demand Ground Level Illumination From a Loitering Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the feasibility of using Laser Excited Phosphor spotlights mounted on loitering unmanned aerial vehicles to provide on-demand illumination to a section of terrain at night. An extensive analysis of existing technology is conducted to select components for such a proposed system. Following this analysis, the deliverable illumination to the ground is determined based on environmental and technological limitations. It is found that a system built from ‘off-the-shelf’ components could plausibly deliver upwards of 50 lx of illuminance on-demand to a user on the ground anywhere within a wide service area of multiple square kilometres.

articleTitle: Boosting Resolution of VHR Remote Sensing Images using CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Remote sensing is increasingly pivotal for security and defense, supporting critical decision-making processes. Achieving high-resolution imagery is essential to enhance the accuracy and reliability of these applications. Pansharpening, a technique that fuses high-resolution panchromatic images with lower-resolution multispectral images to produce high-resolution multispectral data, facilitates more effective ground element detection. Traditional pansharpening algorithms, however, often struggle with local misalignments between panchromatic and multispectral images, leading to artifacts and compromised spectral and spatial fidelity. This paper introduces a novel pansharpening algorithm that mitigates these challenges through an advanced local coregistration technique. By automatically improving the alignment of both inter-and intra-band components during the pansharpening process, our method ensures a more precise and accurate fusion. Additionally, our approach incorporates a super-resolution technique that enhances the resolution of multispectral data up to 15 cm. Experimental evaluations using WorldView-3 satellite images demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, showcasing significant improvements in visual quality and opening new possibilities for advanced remote sensing applications.

articleTitle: Experimental methodology to validate tracked vehicle dynamics models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: An experimental methodology to validate tracked vehicle dynamics through a multibody model is presented. The methodology was conceived and implemented jointly by the Vehicle Dynamics research group of the Politecnico di Torino and Corps of Engineers officers serving at the Italian Army Experimentation Centre (CEPOLISPE). Some original solutions were applied in relation to the impossibility of making any modifications to the tracked vehicle hull. The instrumentation setup permits to measure the motions of the suspended mass (hull), the speed of the sprocket wheels and the displacement of the road wheels that transmit the vehicle dynamics to the tracks. The instrumentation is completed with wiring, connections and fasteners, designed to connect IMU, wire potentiometers and pick-ups to the data acquisition system and power supply. The measurement system was effectively validated through various track tests, leading to the results expected at the design stage. A subset of experimental results with validation is here presented, while a larger set of experimental tests will be later used for the validation of a tracked vehicle multibody model developed in ADAMS ATV software.

articleTitle: Ballistic Missile Threat Modeling and VHF Radar Detection Performance Analysis for Tactical-Level Air Defense Simulator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: In the paper, an approach to ballistic missile threat modeling for surface-to-air missile system (SAMS) personnel tactical-level combat trainer is described. Since air defense ballistic missile warfare is a major challenge from both the technical and decision-making perspective, a multifaceted problem statement to threat modeling is presented to ensure high realism of training scenarios. Furthermore, the exemplary results of the computations performed for a generic medium-range ballistic missile model and VHF radar station are shown.

articleTitle: Conceptual design of the deep-learning-driven flight management system
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This paper presents the usage of image recognition in UAV control systems. This research aims to develop an autonomous control system using deep learning. This system will be tasked with identifying a door within a room and directing the robot towards it. As part of the research, various neural network models and data sets will be tested to determine which provides the highest quality control of the unmanned aerial vehicle.

articleTitle: A Growing Integration of Weaponized Commercial Drones in Battlefield Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Today, the commercial drone industry is one of the fastest-growing industries. The evidence of this is the significant increase in growth and investment in this field. Drone technology has been classified as the most ambitious technology. In this regard, the drone industry is the most convincing example of several new industries, such as agriculture, transportation, etc. With the advancement of drone technology, the growth of the drone industry, and its positive impact on the global drone industry, there is a causal relationship. Recently, these types of drones have been used on the front lines in conflict zones around the world. Many fighters from Myanmar, Ukraine, and Syria are using drone warfare techniques that have been improved in the Russian-Ukrainian war to target, kill, and terrorize civilians based on these tactics. Commercial drones can also provide significant military and intelligence capabilities at a lower cost. Integrating weaponized commercial drones into the larger scheme of the battlefield poses challenges, but their utility is likely to increase in future conflicts. This paper presents the growing cases of commercial and domestic drones used on the battlefield.

articleTitle: Real-Time Control of Multiple Multirotor Platforms Interconnected in a Mesh Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The paper presents an innovative real-time control method for managing a swarm of drones using radio modules operating within a mesh network topology. The method designates one drone as the lead within the system, enabling an organized and coordinated formation. Notably, the arrangement of the drones is highly flexible and can be reconfigured in flight, enhancing adaptability and operational efficiency. The system comprises two primary components: a ground station and an aerial segment. The ground station includes a sophisticated computer system and a router, while the aerial segment is equipped with a drone featuring a Wi-Fi radio link. The paper details this system architecture, providing valuable insights into its functioning and capabilities. Furthermore, the paper highlights the results of tests conducted during actual flights, offering empirical evidence of the system’s performance and reliability. These tests validate the effectiveness of the real-time drone swarm control method, paving the way for its potential application in a wide array of industries and scientific research endeavors. The adaptability and efficiency of the system make it well-suited for a diverse range of use cases, from precision agriculture and infrastructure monitoring to environmental monitoring and wildlife conservation. With its real-time capabilities and adaptable formation management, the meticulously designed drone swarm control system holds significant promise as a foundational framework for various applications. Its potential to be adopted by multiple industries and contribute to cutting-edge scientific research makes it a compelling area for further exploration and development.

articleTitle: Bridging the Gender Gap: Women in Georgia’s Cybersecurity Future
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The rapid growth of technology has brought along an era marked by increasing interconnectedness, while at the same time offering unprecedented opportunities and vulnerabilities. Cybersecurity has become the prime issue for all countries in the world, including Georgia, which is also the case in this instance.This research is a comprehensive study of the current position of cybersecurity in Georgia, with a focus on developing a robust and sustainable cyber ecosystem. The outcomes of this study, which analyzes Georgia’s cybersecurity landscape in the context of government policies, industry initiatives, and academic programs, are crucial for understanding and addressing the cybersecurity workforce shortage, particularly the underrepresentation of women. The research delves into the factors contributing to the gender gap in the cybersecurity field and evaluates the impact of existing projects to bridge this gap.Suggestions include boosting the public-private alliance, allocating cybersecurity education and training funds, and advancing workforce gender equality. Through the measures mentioned and outlined within the research, Georgia will indisputably be the country’s leader in cyber resilience development, and thus, a better digital society will be assured.

articleTitle: Scale Invariant Coherent Change Detection to Locate Micro-Motion in Single Pass SAR Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Micro-Doppler analysis of SAR signals has a broad range of applications including target vibrometry, structural health monitoring, and maritime surveillance. Location of sources of micro-Doppler signals in SAR images is however not straight-forward, where typical artifacts such as ‘ghost’ targets may be unnoticeable if, for example, a vibration is of low amplitude and frequency. This issue is exacerbated by background noise and clutter. A method for locating micro-Doppler signals using scale invariant coherent change detection between subaperture images is developed and tested on SAR data of vibrating targets with a ground truth vibrational frequency of 2 Hz and amplitudes of 16.13 mm and 1.08 mm. The results indicate that this method is promising, where micro-motion from both targets was located and the relative insensitivity of the technique to bright stationary targets is also demonstrated.

articleTitle: Trajectory Backtracking Guidance Control for Head-on Interception of High-Speed Ballistic Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Conventional guidance systems cannot intercept long-range ballistic missiles due to their high re-entry speeds, making them a serious threat to all nations. This paper presents a head-on interception approach for high-speed ballistic threats, requiring the interceptor to backtrack the missile’s trajectory instead of targeting it directly. The approach integrates a look-ahead predictive model to determine the missile’s route and a control model to guide the interceptor. An agent-based, high-fidelity simulation was developed to test the approach under various conditions, incorporating environmental factors such as gravity, air friction, and the Coriolis force. The method was evaluated against short, medium, intermediate-range, and intercontinental missile launches and compared to conventional interception models. The predictive model successfully estimated the missile routes and target points, achieving an interception rate of $81.1 \%$ in intercontinental missile scenarios.

articleTitle: Rapid Radio Frequency Propagation Modelling using a Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This paper examines a novel Machine Learning (ML) Radio Frequency (RF) propagation model optimised for urban environments. In defense applications, RF propagation modelling is crucial for estimating the likely performance of both friendly and adversarial RF systems. Traditional empirical RF propagation models are simple and fast but lack accuracy in complex urban settings due to oversimplified assumptions. Physics-based models that solve aspects of Maxwell’s equations are more accurate but require extensive computational resources and precise scene discretization, making them impractical for rapid modelling large complex areas. To address these limitations, an ML-based approach using a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) is proposed. This ML model functions as an image-to-image translator, converting emitter locations and environmental geometries into RF propagation heat maps. The Pix2Pix GAN architecture, featuring a $\mathbf{U}$-Net generator and PatchGAN discriminator, generates detailed RF maps capturing complex propagation effects like shadowing and channeling. Trained on diverse urban datasets, the model shows an accuracy comparable with physics-based RF propagation models, but with execution speeds that are orders of magnitude faster. The ML model’s efficiency allows for rapid, geometry-specific RF propagation estimates, significantly faster than physics-based models whilst preserving accuracy. This efficiency supports real-time applications, enhancing situational awareness and system optimization in complex environments. In conclusion, the ML-based RF propagation model offers a promising solution for accurate and efficient predictions, leveraging recent advances in generative ML to overcome traditional model limitations and optimize RF system performance in urban scenarios.

articleTitle: Formant Based Direction of Voice for Smart Microphone Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Locating a person by analyzing the direction of their voice and studying the formant frequencies is a fascinating challenge. A person’s formant changes over time, creating a wide-spectrum signal, whereas most direction-finding methods typically require a narrow-band signal. Moreover, the ratio of interelement distance to wavelength $\left(\frac{d}{\lambda}\right)$ varies over time. We track the formant using Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) and Wavelets. We employ a new streamlined easy MUltiple SIgnal Characterization (MUSIC) method to determine the direction. Our research focuses on capturing the formant range and determining the direction using this new approach. This formant stream and Direction of Arrival (DOA) provide crucial Machine Learning data. We have chosen the $\frac{d}{\lambda}$ parameter to be between 0.1 and 0.3, with the interelement spacing at a practical distance for this audio formant frequency. Before conducting accurate data testing, we simulated the array using authentic voices, which presented a significant challenge.

articleTitle: A Multi Agent Simulator for Disaster Prevention and First Response Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The use of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) has exponentially grown in the last decades thanks to their versatility and ease of use. However, deploying a single large drone might not be efficient for completing tasks compared to the use of a heterogeneous swarm of smaller and lighter drones, which can better adapt to different application scenarios and reduce the mission time. In this sense, Search and Rescue (SAR) activities represent an important field of application. Heterogeneous multiagent systems require ad-hoc Guidance, Navigation, and Control (GNC) algorithms to effectively manage the agents of the swarm. Hence, there is a need for an efficient simulator that allows for the validation of such GNC techniques, taking advantage of the positive aspects of a risk-free virtual environment before realworld deployment. In this sense, the main aim of this paper is to propose a heterogeneous Simulink-based multi-agent flight simulator that is able to support researchers in the representation of realistic scenarios before effectively conducting real tests. The effectiveness of the proposed simulator, which is part of the project “CHeMSys: Cooperative Heterogeneous Multi-drone System for disaster prevention and first response,” is evaluated in several scenarios, considering ground, water, and air vehicles.

articleTitle: Machine-learning-enhanced military maintenance management systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Maintenance management systems are essential for ensuring military equipment’s efficient and reliable operation. Adopting advanced technologies, such as machine learning, significantly improves the effectiveness of these systems. These technologies are key in determining the best strategies for military assets’ maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO). Developing well-engineered systems to effectively address challenges, such as detecting patterns, anomalies, and faults with high accuracy and reliability, requires sophisticated software solutions. Most of all, neural networks with predictive capabilities are currently being used to address these challenges. This article overviews maintenance management systems, discussing their main components, functions, and benefits. It examines mainly military systems, including predictive maintenance techniques that use artificial intelligence (AI). The paper reviews each approach, the fundamental concepts, the types of problems these systems are designed to solve, and their overall capabilities.

articleTitle: On Cognitive Radar Jamming for countering Cognitive Electromagnetic Protection systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The paper introduces a novel model of a fully adaptive cognitive radar jamming approach, designed for the purpose of countering modern cognitive radars. Cognitive radar systems have been widely used in modern electromagnetic warfare and also serve as an effective counter to traditional jamming techniques. Cognitive jamming makes use of machine learning and adaptive signal processing strategies to dynamically adapt jamming strategies in response to real-time changes in target radar transmissions. The proposed model may be used to incorporate advanced reinforcement learning algorithms, signal feature extraction techniques, and waveform optimization techniques to create a cohesive system that can optimize jamming strategies with minimal prior knowledge of the electromagnetic environment. The paper also discusses the state-of-the-art in cognitive radar jamming technologies, and their efficiency in the face of intelligent radar equipped with advanced anti-jamming measures. Furthermore, it addresses current challenges and future directions in the field with considerations for defense and security applications.

articleTitle: An innovative air accident investigation method to safety differently
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Flight safety is a paramount for aviation operations; operators, organizations, agencies and authorities are always seeking the state-of-the-art methods, procedures, requirements and processes to reach the safety objectives and standards. The probability of air accidents is significantly low, in line with the number of miles flown and the number of passengers carried. Statistical data, as presented in IATA and ICAO reports, indicate that technological safety in aviation has reached its asymptotic limit, which is a cause for concern given the predicted increase in the number of accidents in the future. The technical reports indicate that, over recent years, there has been a reduction in accidents attributed to technical factors, while accidents with the human factor as the root cause have increased. Consequently, the investigative sector was obliged to adapt to this change by employing increasingly sophisticated analytical techniques and methods. The model proposed is a new accident model, defined as a hybrid. The new hybrid model helps to unravel the mishap causes and it has as its strength the passage through various analyses. To support the proposed model, studies have been conducted on four accident causes that have the human factor as root cause. The proposed model emphasized that everything starts among the organizational system. Furthermore, it came out that training represents a key component of the incident reduction process, enabling the identification and appropriate response to the hazards. Since the human factor that cannot be eliminated, the new method will have limitations, but these can be overcome thanks to the synergetic collaboration of the various described approaches. The work is also intended as a prospective analysis aimed at prevention and preparation for future scenarios, given that it is well known that in the field of technology, we should be able to accept change and find new solutions.

articleTitle: Progressive Optimization of Deep Learning-Based Fight Detection Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Building a fight detection system is essential to enhance public safety and develop automated security surveillance systems. Given the success of deep learning-based models in computer vision and pattern recognition, it is common to use deep convolutional and recurrent neural networks to accurately predict fight scenes. However, the required computational resources hinder the use of these models in memory-limited devices. In this work, we aim to obtain the fight detection model that satisfies both memory constraints and accurate classification performance. First, we design a complex model and then reduce its complexity by leveraging a three-stage progressive model optimization strategy. As a result, we obtained accurate detection models, which are $\sim 2$ and $\sim 5$ times lighter compared to the starting complex model. The experiments are performed using two publicly available datasets, namely Hockey and Movie Fights.

articleTitle: Enhanced GSR Detection By Multispectral Illumination for Forensic Shooting Distance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: In forensic science, measuring the shooting distance is crucial for reconstructing crime scenes involving firearms. This paper evaluates the use of multispectral imaging in the infrared range to enhance the detection and analysis of gunshot residue (GSR) particles on fabric. We analyzed eight white cotton samples shot from distances ranging from 5 to 50 cm. To define the best wavelength, we selected the one where the particles in the image were most contrasted against the fabric, a factor heavily dependent on the color of the fabric. Then, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is applied to multispectral images, at the selected best wavelength, to obtain high-contrast images that significantly improve GSR detection. The polar coordinate transformation aligned the particle analysis with the radial distribution of residues, optimizing the detection process. Our findings indicate that multispectral imaging, especially when combined with advanced image processing techniques, offers a non-invasive measurement method for forensic analysis, providing reliable data that can complement traditional methods.

articleTitle: Cybercity: a Practical Approach to Teach and Learn Cybersecurity in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This paper presents the activities of the Cybercity project. It aims to develop an innovative framework for teaching and learning cybersecurity in a practical way, using an educational platform consisting of a smart city scale model, where the students can practice security threats, attacks and countermeasures. In this paper, the main objectives of the project are presented, and the first activities are discussed. In particular, the design and the implementation of the educational platform are presented.

articleTitle: Potential and Challenges for a Certified Application of Model Reference Adaptive Control to Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The model reference adaptive control (MRAC) framework has proven in an academic context its ability to support complex applications and assure successful results in off-nominal flight conditions. However, this technology is far from being systematically implemented in industrial applications. This paper reflects on some of the challenges hindering this systematic dissemination, and proposes some solutions to be shared by the academic, defense, and industrial communities.

articleTitle: Impact and Mitigation of Index Modulation on Radar Quality for a FMCW-Based Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This study explores how to mitigate the effect of communication on the radar outputs for a radar-centric integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system. The ISAC platform takes the form of an index-modulated frequencymodulated continuous waveform (FMCW) radar. The effects caused by modulating bandwidth and centre frequency on Rangetime and Range-Doppler maps are clearly shown. Several techniques to mitigate different aspects of the effects are motivated and the results are presented. The techniques demonstrate that with increasing computational complexity radar returns can be obtained from the ISAC system of similar quality to the equivalent conventional FMCW. This study demonstrates that ISAC systems can perform communication while not significantly impacting the ability to perform their primary function of sensing.

articleTitle: Preliminary Experimental Results for a Multi-channel Forward Scatter Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This paper reports preliminary experimental tests for a multi-channel Forward Scatter Radar (FSR), namely a FSR system equipped with multiple receiving channels connected to closely spaced antennas. While the majority of the technical literature on FSR focuses on single-channel FSR and exploits signal processing schemes operating in time domain, multichannel FSR has been recently shown to allow target detection and direction of arrival (DoA) estimation by exploiting the signal amplitude modulation that the target induces across multiple antenna elements. Specifically, the theoretical investigations have suggested the use of simple amplitude-based spatial processing schemes to extract the target signature, with tremendous advantages in terms of system complexity. This study aims to validate the theoretical framework by preliminarily demonstrating the practical feasibility of a multi-channel FSR in real-world conditions, with particular reference to an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) scenario. To this purpose, software-defined radios (SDRs) and commercial antennas are employed to transmit orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signals in $\mathbf{S}$ band and several tests are performed with different cooperative targets (e.g., people, drones) moving in the area between the transmitter and the multi-channel receiver. This experimental setup not only provides a first proof of concept for the proposed multi-channel FSR but also enables a preliminary performance comparison between the amplitude-based spatial processing approach and the conventional single-channel FSR that implements time domain processing.

articleTitle: Task priority approach for solving coordination of moving mobile robot in SAR operations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This work describes the application of the Null Space Behavioral technique for the coordinated control of a team of heterogeneous vehicles (quadcopters and tracked ground vehicles) in the presence of obstacles and forbidden zones. This work is part of the ChemSys PRIN PNRR project, in which a heterogeneous team of mobile robots is planned for SAR missions. To solve the problem of coordinated movement of robots in this work, a prioritized approach, the so-called Null Space Based Behavioral Approach, is considered. Specifically, this means that each vehicle is assigned an operational mission in the form of a target region to be reached. The mission is divided into a series of tasks with an assigned priority. The tasks of formation flying and collision avoidance with other vehicles and unknown or moving obstacles are formulated by analytical expressions, as required by the classical null-space behavioral approach. The behavior when approaching the target and avoiding known obstacles is determined by solving a partial differential equation problem within an operational domain. The effectiveness of the proposed technique and the evaluation of possible limitations is discussed on the basis of experimental tests carried out at the Control Systems Laboratory of the Mediterranean University of Reggio Calabria.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Soldier Face Detection and Counting Method for Military Tactical Operations and Artificial Intelligence Powered Weapons
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: In battlefield and tactical operations, automatic detection and tracking of soldiers or military personnel is essential and plays vital roles in soldier presence detection, soldier density calculation, soldier movement tracking, and direction of soldier arrival determination for autonomous robot navigation and war tank direction control, soldier facial expression and emotion analysis, and facial-based soldier authentication. Existing radio frequency (RF) or wireless radios-based soldier localization and tracking approaches suffer from frequent communication failures and heterogeneous channel interferences, and also cannot be used to locate a specific soldier in a particular troop or soldier’s injury conditions. In this paper, we present a YOLOv9 architecture-based soldier face detection and counting method using visual images that can be effectively used for soldier presence detection, tracking, and soldier density calculation. The YOLOv9 face detection (YOLOv9-Face-Detect) model is trained by using a wide variety of face databases having only civilian faces. The trained YOLOv9-Face-Detect model is tested using 250 soldier images having diverse image qualities and soldier density with soldiers wearing different types of personal protective equipment (PPEs), which are taken from public websites. The effectiveness of the YOLOv9-based soldier face detection and counting method was evaluated in terms of the estimated and reference face counts. The method had a mean absolute error of 0.87 and a root mean square error of 2.06 persons per image for the soldier image database, with a model size of 49.2 MB and inference time of 17.66 ms. Evaluation results on the different image qualities demonstrate that the YOLOv9 network-based image analysis can be an effective solution for soldier presence sensing and monitoring applications.

articleTitle: Quality-Aware Rhythm-Aware Heart Rate Variability Analysis for Soldier Health and Wellness Monitoring Using Wearable ECG Sensing Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) derived heart rate variability (HRV) analysis is extensively used in soldier health and emotional state analysis applications by analyzing the variability of the sinus rhythm. In battlefield environments, wearable health monitoring devices may produce noisy ECG signals under electrode movements and muscle contractions that can increase false alarms. Further, HRV analysis is highly affected by the ECG signals with irregular beat-to-beat intervals (BBIs), ectopic beats, and also false positives ($\mathbf{F P s}$) and false negatives (FNs) introduced by the search-back algorithm of the R-peak detector. To alleviate the above-mentioned problems, we propose a quality-aware rhythm-aware HRV (QARA-HRV) analysis system for soldier health and wellness monitoring with reduced false alarms. The proposed QARA-HRV analysis system consists of preprocessing for reducing the baseline wanders and power-line interference, muscle artifacts detection using time-domain ECG features, regular/irregular rhythm recognition using a convolutional network (CNN), and quality-aware rhythm-aware time-domain HVR parameter for normal and abnormal HRV classification. The performance of the QARA-HRV system is evaluated using a wide variety of normal and abnormal ECG signals, and different patterns of artifacts. Evaluation results demonstrate that the quality-aware ECG analysis approach can reduce false alarms under severe muscle artifacts. For the five activation functions, evaluation results showed that the CNN-ReLU-based rhythm recognition method achieved an average SE of $\mathbf{9 2. 4 3 \%}$ and SP of $87.21 \%$ with a model size of 1.6 MB and an average processing time of 0.283 ms. For the untrained ECG databases (single-lead and multi-lead ECG signals), the effectiveness and robustness of the CNN model were demonstrated with signals with different signal-to-noise ratios (SNR of 30 dB and 15 dB). The proposed quality-aware and rhythm-aware HRV analysis system has great potential for smart textiles-based continuous soldier health monitoring with reduced false alarms.

articleTitle: Time-delay approach to coordinate movements of mobile robots subject to uncertainties and external disturbances
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: In this paper, an algorithm for coordinating the robot units of a multi-robot system is proposed. Each robot is modeled as a constrained uncertain system with norm bounded uncertainty subject to external disturbances. The coordination and collision avoidance of the robot platforms is achieved by synchronizing their trajectories, in particular by scheduling the departure times of each platform. The procedure for calculating the time delays consists of two phases: the offline phase and the on-line phase. In the offline phase, the time intervals useful for synchronization are calculated based on the knowledge of the planned trajectories and the maximum trajectory tracking error. The actual delay is calculated in the online phase by solving an optimization problem. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solution, some numerical simulations considering some differential-driven mobile robots in a cluttered and obstacle-rich environment are presented and discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Security Assessment of Drone Teams and Swarms Using an Extended SecRAM Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The growing interest and utilization of drones in both civilian and military contexts has resulted in the deployment of this object in teams and swarms for mission-critical operations. It is evident that standalone drones represent highly exposed cyber-physical systems (CPSs). Furthermore, when they cooperate, they create complex networked CPSs, which could present a multitude of potential attack vectors and points of exploitation. In this study, we present a security risk assessment of drone teams and swarms using an enhanced version of the SESAR Security Risk Assessment Methodology (SecRAM). The study improves SecRAM by integrating model-based notation and including findings from a literature review focused on a particular operational scenario, which involves a network of multiple drones overseen by a mobile edge server using a sandwich methodology.

articleTitle: Blockchain and AI Ethics: Implications for Defence and Security
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: At present, blockchain solutions are drawing the attention of researchers and industrial practitioners due to their potential cross-sectorial applications beyond finance where it emerged, to implement decentralized data handling, guarantee data confidentiality and integrity using cryptography, and create trust in digital data. In Defence, as in other domains, blockchain is a promising solution for manufacturers and suppliers to ‘harden’ the supply chain and logistics by improving operational performance through the entire life cycle, from raw material to retired assets. Furthermore, the decentralized data management has attracted interest to device improved battlefield operations management, border protection, swarm assistance for rescue, as well as military, operations. As the domain is starting to be more dependent on blockchain, and its decentralized and algorithmic-centered decision-making, people are starting the question the ethics of such a solution, following the similar debate around AI applications in general, and in defence also. This paper presents the overall topic and the late conclusions eminent researchers have reached so far.

articleTitle: Open Innovation Model in Military Environments: A Preliminary Case of Aerospace Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Open Innovation (OI), primarily explored in the private sector, has been rooted in theory and practice for many years, demonstrating significant benefits in enhancing competitiveness, creating knowledge, and facilitating the rapid adoption of technologies in real-world settings. OI emphasizes the value of external collaborations, recognizing that diverse industries can converge on strategic points of mutual interest. However, OI has not been widely used in military environments, where protecting classified or confidential information is essential. Therefore in this paper, we present an OI model for military institutions to handle economic constraints and promote the generation of knowledge with technologies applied in defense. The model enables the integration of mission-critical knowledge through rapid prototyping exercises by creating OI ecosystems primarily composed of young researchers that include practices such as crowdsourcing, hackathons, and technological challenges. The model has been built based on three OI events already conducted by the Colombian Air Force (COLAF) and Universidad de los Andes (UNIANDES). Our findings pinpoint crucial factors that accelerate the generation of knowledge, reaching a large number of young researchers who do not typically focus their investigations on defense technology, facilitating successful investments to meet critical military requirements.

articleTitle: Methodological framework design for prediction of swarm movement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The increasing use of drones in military operations, whether for reconnaissance or targeted attacks, poses the problem that anticipating their movements is crucial for defense. The objective becomes even more challenging when predicting the movement of a drone swarm. The paper aims to develop a methodological framework to design an AI-based system able to predict both proximal trajectory and the next possible action against the target. The methodological framework leverages on the Situational Awareness paradigm that addresses the three actions: Perception, Comprehension and Projection. In the Perception phase, the objective must gather the appropriate data. In the Comprehension phase the goal is to design an AI rule-based system able to distinguish what kind of maneuver the drones are going to perform. In the Projection phase the objective is to predict the trajectories and the intention of attack by using Deep Learning Techniques and General AI models respectively.

articleTitle: Black-Box Adversarial ML Attacks on IDS and Multi-Domain Impact Analysis for Threat Intelligence in Automotive Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: In recent years, the automotive sector is going through a period of strong innovation linked to the vehicle connection not only to each other but also to Smart City systems. A direct consequence is an increase in the vehicle attack surface that could lead to complex attacks by providing potential access to a strategic network for government and military organizations for the “Country System”, violating the national security perimeter. The target of these could be the Machine Learning (ML) based Intrusion Detection System (IDS) delegated to protect such assets. Therefore, this research aims to verify the applicability of some Black-Box Adversarial Machine Learning attacks in the CAN bus frame detection task. The victim is a Supervised ML-based IDS assumed to be resident in the vehicle itself. The attack types consist of one evasion and one inference attack.
