The results show the evasion attack impact (weighted accuracy loss) is about ${7 0 \%}$ and the inference attack is not successful. A Multi-Domain (M-D) qualitative impact analysis involving “Cyber” and “Land” domains is proposed in an application scenario of Cyber Warfare and Cyber Espionage constituting integral parts of Multi-Domain Operations (MDOs) potentially aimed at terrorism climates. The victim organization is the entire Nation. This analysis shows the impact of these attacks on real-world assets is very high so a Security by Design approach is needed.

articleTitle: Identification Hardware Attacks of Integrated Circuit Design Data and Intellectual Property
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: It’s critical to comprehend the possible enemies who might launch an assault using the security flaws. This can assist designers in understanding the capabilities of attackers and selecting appropriate countermeasures based on the operation and targeted adversary. The enemy may take the form of an individual or an organized group that wants to get, destroy, or interfere with an asset that they are not authorized to access. Adversaries can be divided into insiders and outsiders when taking into account an integrated circuit design process and the companies involved. A design’s weaknesses can be introduced or exploited more readily by an insider than by an outsider. The biggest difficulty for an outsider to carry out an attack is that they might not always be aware of the design’s internal functions. The functioning of a chip can be reverse engineered by an outsider, although this process takes a lot of time and resources. In this paper we have designed some techniques such as: 1. The pre-silicon, 2. post-silicon security and 3. trust validation techniques to find possible vulnerabilities in a hardware design.

articleTitle: A Model-Based Approach to Failure Mode and Effect Analysis of an Unmanned Quadrotor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: In recent years, the use of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) has exponentially grown in the civil field, thanks to their versatility, ease of use, and the possibility to adopt lowcost electronics. Moreover, the possible application in safetycritical missions reduces the risk to human life. Then, there is an increasing need to develop semi-automatic methods to effectively support traditional models, such as Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) and FailureMode and Effect Analysis (FMEA), for the risk assessment of complex systems, thus reducing the effort required in terms of cost and time. In this paper, we propose a safety assessment procedure to evaluate potential vulnerabilities of the attitude control system of a quadcopter UAV, adopting the MBSA (Model Based Safety Approach) approach based on the quadrotor Simulink model to facilitate FMEA analysis.

articleTitle: A trajectory planning algorithm for a MAV patroller in presence of wind
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This work proposes a solution for the trajectory planning of a micro aerial vehicle (MAV) for patrolling of a cluttered outdoor scenario. Such scenarios are characterized by the presence of unpredictable wind gusts whose effects may hamper the effectiveness of MAV trajectory following. Furthermore, patrolling requires to impose constraints upon tracking error which would, otherwise, reduce both temporal and spatial resolution. By applyinga solution used in trajectory planning for skid-steer tracked vehicles, this work presents an algorithm for the planning of a trajectory which can be tracked by the MAV without violating both actuation and state constraints, even in presence of unknown but bounded external disturbance caused by the presence of wind gusts. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is shown through numerical simulations taking into account a real-world scenario of patrolling in the quay of a seaport.

articleTitle: Exploiting LLMs for E-Learning: A Cybersecurity Perspective on AI-Generated Tools in Education
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: AI and LLM technologies have emerged rapidly, creating more opportunities to develop and enhance e-learning. This paper provides a detailed account of the tools built by the current and future generations of LLMs and AI technologies for creating complex e-learning applications. It introduces the application of these tools, including innovative learning, context-awareness and intelligent learning systems. Moreover, it delves systematically into the security issues of these AI-integrated e-learning environments. The work applies strict research approaches to determine and describe possible risks in system design, data processing, and AI model deployment. We also undertake deeper penetration tests to assess the level of preparedness of these platforms against different types of attacks from the attackers such as attacks targeting the AI components, injection of unverified data and privacy violations. Our study findings reveal the opportunity to apply AI in e-learning, thus highlighting the importance of addressing these concerns. It is a complete guide for the developers and the educational institutions to integrate the LLMs and AI and keep the security strong. This paper adds to the existing literature on the role of AI in education and cybersecurity, providing essential information to the future advancements of safe and innovative e-learning systems.

articleTitle: Integrated Trajectory Planning and Fault Detection for a Skid-Steered Mobile Robot deployed in Post-Disaster Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The development of intelligent response systems for first aid and rescue operations after natural disasters is a rapidly growing field of research. In this paper, we present the ongoing research in the project “CHeMSys: Cooperative Heterogeneous Multi-drone System for disaster prevention and first response”, which addresses the problem of detecting faults that affect the capability of a skid-steered tracked mobile robot in following an assigned trajectory. To achieve this, the dynamics of the trajectory tracking error are reformulated in terms of an uncertain model with norm-bounded uncertainty that accounts for delays in the control loop and possible skidding and slipping phenomena. First, the optimal feasible trajectory for the mobile robot is planned. Then, using some set-based mathematical properties of the feasible trajectory, a multivariate logic with low computational complexity is used to detect the faults and a reconfiguration strategy is applied in case of a sensor fault. The algorithm has been shown to be effective in distinguishing actuator faults from faults in the robot’s measurement system and is based on set-theoretic arguments. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solution, we present the results of several numerical simulations performed with a simulator implemented in the MATLAB/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Evaluating Startle in Aviation: A Focus on Instrumentation and Measurement Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The phenomenon of startle in aviation is a critical area of study, particularly due to its implications for pilot performance and aviation safety. Startle responses can significantly impair cognitive functioning and decision-making processes during unexpected in-flight events. This impairment can lead to inappropriate pilot responses, which may arise from a mismatch between perceived stimuli and the active mental framework the pilot is employing. Such mismatches can be exacerbated by stress and the complexity of modern aviation systems. This overview investigates the main technological tools and data analysis methodologies employed for startle identification in aviation.

articleTitle: Practical Approach for Processing and Fusion of Multimodal Data for Reconnaissance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Processing and fusion of multimodal reconnaissance data is critical in the context of intelligence gathering and decision support. We examine the implementation of a suitable architecture and demonstrate the processing and data fusion by exploiting AI-based transcription, translation and Large Language Model information extraction components using audio and text data. We also highlight the potential benefits and challenges of integrating them into intelligence workflows. A possible categorisation of data processing and fusion components according to their practical role is provided.

articleTitle: Cyber Social Security in Multi-Domain Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Multi-Domain Operations (MDO) is a military strategy that is being widely adopted integrating capabilities from multiple domains to generate a synergistic effect. It is characterized by actions conducted across different domains and contested environments to neutralize adversary’s strengths. The paper presents a logical architecture along two dimensions: Horizontal and Vertical. The Horizontal dimension is characterized by the five domains of MDO (i.e., Maritime, Land, Air, Space, Cyber). Instead, the Vertical dimension identifies the three security operating units: Detection, Response and Prevention. Leveraging the new knowledge gained in each domain, the intersection between these two dimensions allows to redefine detection rules in MDO, formulate new response plans and prevent both known and emerging security threats. Additionally, this work explores the intersection among Artificial Intelligence (AI) and cybersecurity, emphasizing the benefits of integrating these technologies to enhance defense capabilities.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Solutions for Cybersecurity in Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The research highlights the importance of cyber security in the energy sector, focusing on how artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) can make power grids more reliable and secure, particularly in Ukraine. The study looks at how energy systems are vulnerable to cyberattacks, especially during the Russia-Ukraine war, which has caused major disruptions in Ukraine’s energy supply. The research includes a detailed analysis of recent cyber attacks on Ukraine’s power systems, exploring how AI and ML can detect and prevent these threats in real-time, and how effective these technologies are at protecting critical infrastructure. The key findings suggest that AI and ML are essential for predicting and reducing cyber threats, improving energy production and distribution, and keeping power systems running despite increasingly complex cyber attacks. This study is the first in a series of papers on this topic. The research emphasizes the need for a well-organized cyber security approach and the adoption of AI-based solutions to strengthen energy security against modern threats.

articleTitle: Cuffless Blood Pressure Stratification and Hypertension Recognition Using Wearable PPG Sensor for Continuous Soldier Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Continuous hypertension monitoring plays a vital role in soldier health assessment management of the health of military veterans in combat-exposed and combat-injured situations and post-battlefield stress management. The cuff-based blood pressure (BP) measurement devices can provide accurate hypertension assessment but cannot enable continuous hypertension analysis for soldiers and military veterans. Therefore, in this paper, we present a cuffless BP classification method for monitoring hypertension by using the photoplethysmography (PPG) signal because of its non-invasive and low-cost sensing. By considering the devices’ constraints, we attempt to present a lightweight BP classification method for recognizing hypertension events by using PPG waveform features and traditional machine learning (ML) classifiers without using multi-modal cardiac signals and computationally expensive deep learning networks. On a wide variety of PPG signals taken from standard databases, evaluation results show that the random forest-based BP classification method had a classification accuracy of ${9 2. 0 4 \%}$ and also hypertension recognition accuracy of ${9 3. 7 8 \%}$ as compared to the eight ML classifiers-based methods. From our results, it is observed that the performance of the PPG features-based BP classification and hypertension recognition methods may be degraded under ambulatory PPG recordings in the presence of severe motion artifacts in addition to the pathological PPG signals.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Cognitive Load of Pilots: A Review of Workload Assessment Tools and Data Analysis Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Cognitive workload (CWL) assessment plays a pivotal role in ensuring safety and performance in aviation. This review provides an in-depth examination of the various methods used to evaluate cognitive workload, with a particular focus on aircraft pilots. The methodologies discussed encompass subjective ratings, task performance, behavioral, and physiological measures. Each technique is analyzed for its effectiveness, limitations, and applicability to real-world aviation scenarios. The convergence of multiple methods, particularly the integration of physiological measures such as heart rate variability (HRV) and electroencephalography (EEG), provides the most robust approach to cognitive workload assessment.

articleTitle: Measuring the risk of evasion and poisoning attacks on a traffic sign recognition system
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Nowadays, one of the most important applications of machine learning is autonomous vehicles that employ driver assistance technologies to facilitate driving or remove the need for the human operator. As a result, different machine learning models, such as traffic sign recognition systems, are useful to help the vehicle change the driving style based on the scenario. In this context, the systems are vulnerable to different kinds of adversarial attacks, such as evasion and poisoning, that can compromise the security and integrity of these systems, as well as the safety of passengers. These types of attacks involve corrupting a model’s training process, compromising its future use. In addition, since these algorithms acquire images from multiple sensors, it is important to investigate attacks that could compromise the detection of Machine Learning or Deep Learning models to prevent civilian and military autonomous vehicles from being compromised and thus generating false information or misclassifications. Therefore, the paper presents an experimentation of black-box evasion and poisoning attacks called Zeroth-Order Optimization (ZOO) and BadNets on a traffic sign recognition CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) by using optimization techniques to maximize the attacks’ performance. The goal is to measure the risks linked to these attacks in the autonomous automotive field and check their efficiency compared to the chosen model.

articleTitle: Feasibility of Deploying a Vertical Chain of Multicopter Drones along a Shared Tether to Provide a Stratospheric High Altitude Platform Station
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This paper gauges the feasibility of deploying a long chain of multicopter drones, spaced out vertically along a shared powerline tether, to establish a high altitude platform station in the stratosphere. A station-keeping platform high in the stratosphere with continual access to plentiful electrical power offers various capabilities in the defense and security ambit: for instance, remote observation for search and rescue missions. To screen the feasibility of deploying multicopter drones in this way, several key design parameters are enumerated here, including: estimating the required total drone power consumption; the lateral forces imposed by strong winds at altitude; and dimensioning the propellers to perform in rarefied stratospheric air. Outlined solutions to these challenges are provided and the initial high-level system design suggests that there is potential to deploy a high altitude platform station in this new manner.

articleTitle: A Comparative Scoping Study of Local and Regional Museum Storage Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This study examines the advantages and disadvantages of smaller local museum storage facilities versus larger regional storage complexes, with a particular focus on the long-term preservation and security of artworks. The research aims to determine which storage model better suits the needs and resources of different national museum systems, and to identify sustainable solutions for artworks storage. The analysis primarily employs qualitative methods, including interviews and case studies. The findings indicate that smaller local storages offer quick and cost-effective solutions that well serve local communities, while regional storage complexes provide greater capacity and higher security levels in the long term, though they come with higher initial costs and longer implementation times. The research suggests a hybrid approach that combines the modernization of smaller storages with the establishment of one or more regional storage complexes, taking into account long-term sustainability, artwork security, and economical energy management.

Author Keywords: Public Collection Storage and Storage Security

articleTitle: Preliminary Concept Design of an Ontology for the Security Risk Assessment of U-Space Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: The ever-growing risks of cyberattacks are a major security concern for drone-based applications in U-space, which potentially lead to increasing vulnerabilities and threat scenarios. This necessarily calls for the assessment of security risks in U-space solutions. Moreover, automated security risk assessment shall be explored for facing the U-space complexity and improve cost-efficiency in engineering secure systems. For this purpose, ontologies may effectively support the formal knowledge representation of security-related aspects in U-space and for automating some assessment steps with proper inference rules. This paper proposes a preliminary concept design of a cybersecurity ontology that will integrate and correlate the specification of different information to be used in assessing the security risk of U-space solutions.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Microgrids Design Tools: an Area of Development for New Decision Support Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Homer (Hybrid Optimization of Multiple Energy Resources) Pro is a robust energy modeling software developed to support the design and optimization of microgrids and distributed energy systems. Xendee is another commercial concurrent software, available in the cloud. There are many others microgrids’ design tools, offering slightly different functionalities, such as REOPT, DERCAM (Xendee’s forerunner), Microgrid Planner. They work to help microgrids designers with feasibility studies. Designs (in Homer) and projects (in Xendee) are the way to run different configurations and get results, that are comparable, especially in terms of economic indicators. However, despite their great capabilities, they lack a flexible tool to help the comparison in terms of operational flexibility and compound indicators, supporting resilience analysis. This paper shows how the results of a feasibility study, carried out using the above-mentioned software, can be integrated, or simplified and replaced by a novel decision support tool, providing the designer several degrees of freedom, thus making a comparative choice when resilience is the focus.

articleTitle: A Preliminary Concept for a Resilience Service to Manage Drone Cyber-Physical Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Drones operating at very low level are posing complex multi-domain risks, which may be traced back to both safety and (cyber)security risks. The management of all these risks is essential to achieve the safety and security objectives of U-space in regard to the drone ecosystem. This requires the exploration of technical feasibility for managing non-cooperative drones and the analysis of their impact on the current U-space system services. This work proposes a preliminary concept for improving the safety and the security of a U-space system by means of a novel service, named DARS (Drone Attack Resilience Service). The service explicitly relies on resilience-driven features and is powered by artificial-intelligence capabilities. The preliminary concept is discussed in terms of U-space impacts, context and functional architecture.

articleTitle: Evaluation of drone pilots’ sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous system responses during simulated flight in familiar and unfamiliar environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This paper presents an in-depth analysis of drone pilots’ autonomic nervous system responses. The study focuses on the sympathetic and parasympathetic responses elicited during drone flights in familiar and unfamiliar environments. The research uses electrocardiogram (ECG) data to quantify the pilots’ physiological responses. The ECG, a widely used and noninvasive tool, provides valuable insights into heart electrical activity, reflecting the dynamic balance between the sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. This data is crucial in understanding the physiological changes in pilots’ minds in various flight conditions and forms the basis of our analysis. In flights in the known environment, the study observes a predominance of parasympathetic activity, indicative of a relaxed and focused state. It is characterized by a decrease in heart rate, a standard marker of parasympathetic activation. Pilots exhibit a state of calm alertness, which is necessary for precise control and successful navigation. In contrast, on flights in an unknown environment, there is a marked increase in sympathetic activity, as evidenced by the rise in heart rate. This heightened arousal is a typical “fight or flight” response, preparing the pilot for potential challenges or threats in an unfamiliar environment. The study also explores the implications of these findings for drone pilot training and performance optimization. Understanding the physiological responses to various flight conditions can inform targeted interventions to manage stress and enhance performance. For example, stress management techniques such as biofeedback, which helps pilots monitor and control their physiological responses, and mindfulness, which can improve their focus and attention, could be incorporated into training programs to help pilots better regulate their autonomic responses. In conclusion, this article provides novel insights into drone pilots’ sympathetic and parasympathetic responses in various flight environments. The findings underscore the importance of considering drone operation’s physiological and psychological aspects, with significant implications for training, performance, and safety in the rapidly evolving field of drone technology.

articleTitle: UAV test-bench platform for propeller diagnostics using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This paper presents a test platform for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles, capable of detecting early damages in UAV components. The paper presents the architecture of the platform and the machine learning method used to detect damages. The method was proven with two types of emulated damages on propellers. The results showed a classification accuracy of about $90 \%$ in the identification of the damage.

articleTitle: Advanced Monitoring with Enhanced Security in Critical Infrastructures: the DOSSIER framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Current monitoring procedures for critical infrastructure, especially in structural health, primarily rely on manual inspections, which require physical contact and are often laborintensive, time-consuming, and costly. Visual observations dominate these inspections. Smart and secure sensing solutions based on the Internet of Things can significantly improve monitoring for critical infrastructures like bridges, roads, and smart grids.The DOSSIER framework aims to enhance health monitoring of critical infrastructures through non-invasive, advanced sensor networks and heterogeneous data sources to evaluate infrastructure conditions and detect anomalies. The framework’s objectives include data acquisition from multiple and heterogeneous sources, adopting predictive models to provide early warnings, and implementing rule-based processing of acquired information. Additionally, DOSSIER aims to extend the service life of existing infrastructures by reducing the impact of anomalies, including those resulting from attacks.

articleTitle: A Cognitive-Based ISAR System for Spectral Compatibility Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This paper proposes and analyzes the concept of a cognitive inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) ensuring spectral compatibility in crowded electromagnetic environments. In such a context, cognitive radar system alternates between a perception stage, recognizing possible emitters in its frequency range, and an action stage, synthesizing and transmitting a tailored radar waveform to achieve the desired task while guaranteeing the spectral coexistence with overlaid emitters. The perception stage is carried out by an electronic support measurement system (ESM) that senses the environment and extracts relevant spectral parameters. The action stage employs a tailored signal design process, synthesizing a radar waveform with bespoke spectral notches, enabling ISAR imaging over a wide spectral bandwidth without interfering with the other radio frequency (RF) systems. A key enabling technology for the proposed application is the compressed sensing (CS) framework, allowing accurate ISAR imaging even with missing data in the frequency domain (induced by spectral notches) and in the slow-time dimension (enabling the system to perform additional RF activities). The capabilities of the proposed system are assessed exploiting a dataset of drone measurements in the frequency band [13, 15] GHz. The results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed system to enable the spectral compatibility while delivering high-quality ISAR images.

articleTitle: Exploring the RCS of In-Flight UAVs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: This paper presents a first-order statistical analysis of the Radar Cross Section (RCS) of consumer and professionalgrade in-flight drones. The study is based on measurements collected in a rural environment using an X-band Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar system during the simultaneous flight of two drones. A detailed description of the experimental setup and data preprocessing, including the RCS estimation procedure is provided. Subsequently, the RCS fluctuations for each drone are characterized by fitting the RCS data to various one- and two-parameter statistical models. The results show that different drones exhibit distinct RCS fluctuation patterns, with each drone conforming to different statistical models, reflecting differences in their size and structural complexity. These findings have significant implications for the development of tailored radar signal processing algorithms aimed at enhancing drone detection and tracking performance.

articleTitle: Predicting Operator Situation Awareness from Psychophysiological Signals: Utility of Personalized and Universal Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Demanding operational environments require humans to team effectively with autonomy. Unobtrusive and objective estimates of human situation awareness (SA) can facilitate effective human-autonomy teaming. We conducted an experiment in which 15 subjects completed a spacecraft piloting simulation. Psychophysiological data were collected during each trial of the experiment along with post-trial questionnaire measures of SA. We created models of SA using psychophysiological responses and compared the predictive performance of Personalized models to Universal models fit from all subjects. The Universal model root mean square error (RMSE) was within $6 \%$ of the total range of the scale, while the Personalized model was $4.7 \%$. Model predictive performance was consistent with these results, with Personalized models only slightly outperforming the Universal models, and each with an increase in RMSE by a fraction of a point. This work demonstrates an ability to accurately capture human cognitive states in an operationally relevant task.

articleTitle: Addressing ionospheric impairments in the azimuth ground displacements retrieved by using SAOCOM-1 L-band SAR data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving scenario of the L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellite systems, it is crucial to mitigate ionospheric effects that can strongly corrupt the ground displacements retrieved through Differential SAR Interferometry (DInSAR), Multi Aperture Interferometry (MAI), and Pixel Offset Tracking (POT) methods. The purpose of this study is to emphasize the importance of reducing these impairments. In particular, this work shows how the presence of the ionosphere in SAR images may generate local subpixel offsets in the azimuth position, thus affecting the SAR image’s co-registration procedure and, consequently, the surface displacement measurements. The impact of this misregistration appears like “azimuth streaks” in the displacement maps retrieved with POT and MAI techniques. The displacement analysis that highlights the impact of the ionospheric effects has been conducted on the eruption of the Litli-Hrùtur volcano in Iceland, by using StripMap L-band SAR images acquired by the Argentinian SAOCOM-1 constellation.

articleTitle: Not Sure Your Car Withstands Cyberwarfare
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Data and derived information about target victims has always been key for successful attacks, both during historical wars and modern cyber wars. Ours turns out to be an era in which modern cars generate a plethora of data about their drivers, and such data could be extremely attractive for offenders. This paper seeks to assess how well modern cars protect their drivers’ data. It pursues its goal at a requirement level by analysing the gaps of the privacy policies of chief automakers such as BMW and Mercedes with respect to the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). It is found that both brands are still imprecise about how they comply with a number of GDPR articles, hence compliance often results non-verifiable. Most importantly, while BMW exhibits slightly broader compliance, both brands still fail to comply with a number of relevant articles of the regulation. An interpretation of these findings is a nonnegligible likelihood that your car may turn against you should cyberwarfare break out.

articleTitle: Conceptual, Functional and Operational Interactions of ATC Radars and Navigation Systems in the Framework of Future Airspace Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Radar-based Air traffic control (ATC) and navigation systems play a pivotal role in current and future airspace management scenarios. With respect to their traditional tasks -i.e., detection and localization of a target, modern radar systems exploit cutting edge technologies for enhanced capabilities. The most notable innovation is Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) radar, which allows for rapid scanning of the surveillance volume, better target discrimination and improved resistance to jamming, contributing to enhanced situational awareness. ATC systems are evolving into complex networks with real-time data processing capabilities, integrating automation, artificial intelligence and machine learning, with a data-driven approach enhancing decision-making and enabling efficient routing through optimization of schedules and resources. This paper outlines the cooperative interactions between surveillance technologies and navigation systems, exploring the technologies and the system architectures for ATC and air traffic management (ATM). Current surveillance technologies and radionavigation systems are analyzed in terms of strengths and weaknesses, performance characteristics and their impact on Communication, Navigation and Surveillance (CNS) avionics systems developed for mission-and safety-critical applications.

articleTitle: Multiple approaches for studying energy systems cybersecurity issues
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Workshop on Technologies for Defense and Security (TechDefense)
abstract: Energy systems are increasingly becoming a set of power technologies, digital devices and communication equipment. They constitute strategic infrastructures that are often physically and cybernetically attacked. In recent years, cyber attacks have become real attack weapons, affecting countries activities. Academia, industries and security agencies are proposing and implementing different solutions to face these criticalities. In this context, Italian national agency for new technologies, energy and economic sustainable development (ENEA) and University of Naples “Federico II” participate to “Cyber Security of Energy Systems” project, funded by the Italian Ministry of the Environment and Energy Security. The aim of the project consists in identifying novel systems, approaches and solutions to prevent energy systems cyber attacks. To achieve this goal, ENEA and University of Naples researchers are investigating the impacts of cyber attack in smart grid (and microgrid) equipped with classical and quantum communication studying the use Clifford quantum channels for the purpose of cybersecurity.
